note: Boulders (Dave 2026-10-21): not rocks; a pick (or an axe, half as fast) breaks them into rough stones. The yield is plain math from the size: volume (an ellipsoid of the boulder's radius and height_ratio x radius high, the buried part included) x density x yield, divided by the mass of one stone (weights.json, 0.5 kg since Dave 19 Nov 2026), is the number of stones; a 1 m radius boulder makes about 870, 0.3 m about 23, 1.2 m about 1,500 at yield 0.047. STONES PER BLOW (tools; Dave 12 Nov 2026, TEST-013: "a stone pickaxe ... at least 1 rock per swing and higher tiers more rocks per swing ... destroy the rock faster and still get the same amount of rock while degrading the durability less for higher tiers") are by the tool class and material (items.json) of the tool IN HAND, which must be on the hotbar: pick stone 1, bronze 2, iron 3, steel 4. 14 Nov 2026 (GOALS-REPAIR R2b): copper pick 1.5 and copper axe 0.75, between stone and bronze, PROVISIONAL (GOALS-REPAIR A-14). A fraction carries over between blows (the boulder's progress). Every blow wears the tool once (drops.json tool_wear rock), so a better pick wears less for the same stone. An axe is the wrong tool: half the pick's stones of its material, and tool_wear rock wears it 5 per blow. On bare rock (server_items _mine, 23 Nov 2026) the class's rates are lifted so its stone tool gives one a blow (an axe: 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5), so every tier breaks more than the one below. A steel hammer 2.5 (was 2, the same as iron; tier consistency, coordinator 23 Nov 2026: a better tool is always better at its job). The stones in a boulder are fixed by its size whatever the tool. Each piece rolls its own luck double, ore and flint. The boulder shrinks as stones come out (src/shared/boulder_wear.gd: its radius falls in a straight line with the share left, to a fifth at the last stone; cracks from the first blow; Dave 21 Nov 2026) and is gone with the last one; what is left is saved (world_items.json boulders). Every blow wears the tool like other work (durability in items.json, drops.json tool_wear per_use may add more). Boulders are server-owned and laid out like loose stones: per 32 m cell, up to max_per_cell, only where the ground rises more than min_slope or at a water bank, deterministic from the cell. size: radius_min..radius_max, radius_power > 1 makes small ones commoner. luck_extra: the chance that a blow's stone comes away as two (and takes two from the boulder), passed through the luck function (0 switches it off; 0.05 means about 5 percent at luck 0, about 7 percent at +10, 3.5 percent at -10).
ore_yield_note: A rock with an ore (copper, tin, iron, coal or salt: boulders.json ore items, and the copper and tin ore_rocks; limestone, chalk and marble rocks are stone and use yield) holds stones at this rate, as every rock did from 19 Nov 2026; plain stone rocks use yield. Dave 21 Nov 2026 asked for fewer stones from plain rocks only and for copper and tin to stay abundant (BugsList 118), so ore rocks keep their amounts and a big one still holds thousands.
yield_note: Dave 21 Nov 2026 play test (BugsList 118: "so far I have mined over 3200 stones from this big rock and it feels accessive. it also hasnt shrunk any that we can see."): PROVISIONAL BW-4 0.047 for plain stone rocks (ore rocks: ore_yield), so the biggest common boulder (radius 1.2 m, 2.4 m across) holds about 1,500 stones and every size keeps the same stones per volume: radius 1.0 about 870, 0.75 about 370, 0.5 about 110, 0.3 about 23, 0.25 about 13. Saves scale what is left in worked boulders by the change (boulder_per_kg). Before that: Dave 19 Nov 2026 (boulders PLAN.md section 3: "lets make stones 0.5kg and when you break bigger rocks you loose some material just to dust and smaller bits that are lost ... into 0.5kg bits with about 30% loss of material"; "I don't want that video game thing where a bold just gets broken in 5 minutes"): 0.7 of the rock's weight comes away, in 0.5 kg stones (weights.json), so a rock 1 m across (radius 0.5) gives about 1,620 and one 2 m across about 12,960; stones per blow are unchanged. Before that, BugsList_Current.md entry 3 (Dave 18 Nov 2026: a rock yielded hundreds of stones without shrinking): the share of a boulder's mass that comes away as 1 kg stones, 0.5 until 18 Nov (a 1.2 m rock held over 7000). PROVISIONAL RK-1: 0.04, so the stones stay proportional to the rock's volume (a 0.3 m rock about 10, a 0.6 m one about 80, a 1.2 m one about 640) and each blow visibly cracks and shrinks it.

ore.note: Ore and coal from boulders (guide finding F-23, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): a boulder that lies within reach_m of an ore body of the terrain (the geology's ore_bodies) is an outcrop with that ore with chance boulder_share (decided from the boulder's key, so it is the same every time). A PICK (not an axe) takes the ore: each piece that comes away is the ore with chance piece_share, else stone. Iron needs no better pick than copper: there is no bronze pick in the game, and an iron pick needs iron ore first (a circle), so the ladder is made by rarity, not by tool. items: ore name in data/tables/resources.json -> item id. 2026-10-31 (Sal): `needs_material` lists which pick materials may take each ore (14 Nov 2026, GOALS-REPAIR R2b: a Copper pick takes what a stone one does, not iron; master s2 "Bronze mines Iron"): coal, copper and tin with any pick, iron only with a bronze, iron or steel pick, so the ladder is stone pick (copper, tin, coal) -> forge -> bronze ingot -> bronze pickaxe -> iron. The server reads needs_material in _hit_boulder (checked 3 Nov 2026), so a stone pick cannot take iron. 2026-11-10 (Steve, Jamie's tin check): a compact ore body (lens, halo, pipe, vein, placer) within reach_m comes first, the nearest of them; else a coal seam or other layer of the province under the boulder counts only where one of its bands lies within layer_depth_m under the bedrock surface. Bodies of ores not in items (gems, flint) are skipped instead of hiding the rest. 10 Nov 2026 (coordinator, item_system.md): rock salt. An evaporite salt bed (a layer) shows in boulders where its band comes within layer_depth_m of the bedrock surface, and a salt dome (a pipe) only where its top does; its pieces are the same Salt as sea salt, with any pick. 10 Nov 2026 (Steve, Dave's seven building tiers: Concrete = Lime powder + Sand + Stone): a boulder that is not an ore outcrop is of its own bedrock (TileTerrainData.bedrock_name_at, the layered rock at the bedrock surface under it). Over a rock in `rocks` (rock name -> item) a share rock_boulder_share of the boulders (from the key) give that item: each piece a pick takes is it with chance rock_piece_share, else stone; any pick material. Limestone, chalk and marble all give Limestone.
ore.hammer_note: Dave 15 Nov 2026 (TREE_WOOD_TOOLS_DESIGN.md s1, W-12): the Stone Hammer breaks rock and takes copper, tin, coal, salt and limestone like a stone pick; iron ore still needs a bronze or better PICK (pick_only). A Wooden hammer does not break rock (no tools.hammer.wood rate).
ore.finds_note: Finds broken out of a pocket rock (distribution pockets): the row's ore -> the item. Kept apart from items so the geology's gold, silver and gem bodies do not turn boulders into outcrops of them.

ore_rocks.note: One rule for copper AND tin rocks (Dave 21 Nov 2026, play test: "both copper and tin should be placed along or close to rivers being more abundant and bigger near the mountains and smaller and less abundant closer to the ocean but they should both be there. they should even have a small chance of randomly being almost anywhere"; "they should also be very abundant if they are right over an ore vein of their type"). copper_rocks and tin_rocks below take every value here and add their own slot and grade (server_items._ore_rock_cfg). Per 32 m cell, from the cell's own stream named after the ore (server_items._lay_out_ore_rocks), `tries` spots and one more for the mountain-foot boulder. Upland u, 0..1, from the ground height at the spot: 0 at or under upland_low_m (the coastal plain), 1 at upland_high_m and over (the foothills and valleys under the mountains). A spot in water no deeper than bed_depth_m (a river or lake bed) or on a dry bank within bank_reach_m of water takes a rock with chance lerp(water_chance_coast, water_chance_mountain, u); anywhere else on dry land with chance `chance`; never in deeper water. Over a body of its own ore (the geology within body_reach_m: one look for the cell first, then the spot), every spot takes a rock with chance at least body_chance, wherever it lies, and u is raised by body_upland. Size share s = size draw x lerp(size_coast, 1, u): under hand_share it is a loose ore picked up by hand, above it a rock to break, radius_min..radius_max over the rest (0.5 to 2 m across, Dave 17 Nov 2026), so rocks are smaller and mostly hand pieces by the sea and up to 2 m by the mountains. foot: the last try, a big boulder with chance foot.chance on gentle ground (rise per metre under max_slope) where the ground climbs more than rise_m within reach_m (at most 26 m, inside the prefetched pad). All values PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md For Dave OR-1..OR-6.
ore_rocks.chance_note: Dave 27 Nov 2026, the layered cake: copper and tin as small rocks across their whole layer, dry land too, not only by water (BugsList 186): 2.5% a try on dry land inside the area (was 1%), about one small rock every 80 m; still scaled by the area, so none on the beach. PROVISIONAL CR-11.

copper_rocks.note: Copper rocks (Dave 16 Nov 2026, his photo of real copper ore: rough rocks wholly coated in green to blue-green malachite, fist size to boulders). Laid out by the shared ore_rocks rule (Dave 21 Nov 2026). Server rows like boulders with ore copper, mined the same way (a pick or the Stone Hammer, any material); a loose piece picked up by hand is Copper ore. grade_min..grade_max (from the rock's key): the share of its pieces that are copper ore, so the copper in a rock is its size times its grade; every copper outcrop boulder of the geology gets a grade too, in place of ore piece_share. slot: the cell's slots from 8 (15 the mountain-foot boulder). PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md CR-6.

tin_rocks.note: Tin rocks (Dave 17 Nov 2026, his photo of cassiterite: pale speckled granite with white quartz veins carrying dark brown-black crystals; river pebbles glassy, plum size). Laid out by the shared ore_rocks rule (Dave 21 Nov 2026), exactly like copper; before that only by water within 80 m of a tin body, so a river away from tin geology had none. grade_min..grade_max: share of a boulder's pieces that are Tin ore. Slots 16..23 of the cell (23 the mountain-foot boulder). PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md TN-5.

iron_rocks.note: River iron stones (Dave 21 Nov 2026: "there are reddish brown rocks everywhere normally so iron should be a common thing to find a long river bed as well"; "river iron rocks should be the same size as a rounded iron ingot and they are pickable so you gather them by hand"; "if there are any larger than that they need to be broken down like anormal rock with a pick bronze or better. 1 ingot sized iron rocks will be 50% of the stones out there, 30% of them should be double that size and 20% can be triple sized"). Laid out by the shared ore_rocks rule like copper and tin, but commoner (chance on dry land, water_chance_coast and water_chance_mountain set here over the shared values), over an iron body too. sizes [[share, ores], ...] by the size draw (server_items._lay_out_ore_rocks): one ore is a loose Iron ore stone picked up by hand; two or three is a small rock of that volume (ingot_radius_m for one ore), all Iron ore (ore_only: that many Iron ore and no stone, and a tool that cannot take iron is refused, so it is not ground to stone), broken with a bronze or better pick (ore pick_only, needs_material). No mountain-foot boulder. outcrops_unchanged: the geology's iron outcrop boulders keep ore piece_share and their own size. Slots 24..30 of the cell. PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md IR-1.

meteorite_rocks.note: Iron-nickel meteorites (Dave 21 Nov 2026: "lets have meteors about half as frequent as rocks because they have been falling for millions and billions of years. they break into iron chunks that count as iron ingots"). Read as half as often as iron rocks on open ground, the same everywhere (they fall from the sky, so no more by rivers or mountains and no ore body): on the shared ore_rocks rule with chance 0.015 a try anywhere (shallow water too), no water chances, no body, no mountain-foot boulder, full size everywhere (size_coast 1). A loose piece picked up by hand is an Iron chunk; a meteorite to break, radius_min..radius_max (40 to 70 cm across), breaks with any pick or the Stone Hammer (no needs_material, not pick_only) and holds stones at the plain boulder yield, not ore_yield (plain_yield: a lump of metal, not a big ore rock), each piece an Iron chunk with chance grade, else stone. Slots 32..39 of the cell. Look: ore_rock_look meteorite. PROVISIONAL, docs/design/COPPER_ROCKS.md MT-1.

rock_fields.note: Rocky ground (Dave 26 Nov 2026, thread 'Place rocks and boulders on mountains': "did we ever start putting rocks and boulders on and around mountains where they should be"; the boulders plan of 19 Nov 2026, sections 6 to 8). server_items.gd _lay_out_rock_fields lays these per 32 m scatter cell on top of the plain boulders and ore rocks, under their own keys (FIELD_KEY), so older boulders and worked rocks keep their places. Mountain rocks come in CLUSTERS: a big core rock (radius by kind) with satellites[0..1] smaller ones round it, each satellite_share of the core's radius, out to satellite_spread core radii past its edge. Kinds of cluster: scree at the foot of steep ground (the ground climbs more than scree_rise_m within relief_reach_m of the cluster; full at twice that; on ground of at most scree_flat_max rise a metre), up to scree_clusters a cell, cores up to scree_wall_size times bigger under a high wall; rocky ground above treeline_m (the tiles' treeline), faded in from treeline_fade_m below to treeline_full_m above, up to high_clusters; hilltop outcrops where the cell's middle stands top_drop_m over all four sides, up to top_clusters, only on the crown (no more than top_near_m below the middle). Rounded rocks in water no deeper than water_bed_m or on a bank within water_bank_m, up to water_rocks a cell by water, scaled by water_journey from the sea (first) to the headwaters (second); a lone giant (erratic) on open gentle ground away from water with chance erratic.chance a cell, not on the low coastal flats (below erratic.min_height_m). Mountain kinds come in patches: patch noise patch_m across, patch_share of the land thick, the rest at the kind's patch_floor share. radius_power > 1 makes small ones commoner. Crags: where the cell is steep (its rise per metre across relief_reach_m, faded in over crag.from), up to crag.clusters a cell (crag.patch_floor off the patches), not on the low coast (below crag.min_height_m): on a spot steeper than steepest only a crag stands, angular, tilted to the face and set into it by crag.sink_share of its radius, no apron, up to crag.steepest. No loose rock on ground steeper than steepest (rise per metre; a giant 0.3 of it); a rock on a slope is set into it by sink_share of the drop across it (rise times radius), so its low side meets the ground; no two rocks of a cell overlap (older boulders included); nothing within keep_clear_m of anything built, a fire or a player standing there as the cell is laid (loose stones too), none in a camp's kept ground. A mountain rock of apron_from_m radius or more is drawn by the client in an apron of broken stones (look only: no rows, no collision). loose_per_cluster: loose stones to pick up round each cluster (at most 64 a cell). density_scale multiplies every count (the measure job tries other values). PROVISIONAL RF-2 (26 Nov 2026): the first measure cut the counts for the world sync's cost; the pictures then read bare (small rocks, too few); thrice the rocks still read bare and cost 214 ms a second of sync at 32 players, so the coordinator asked for fewer, bigger, clustered rocks: clusters with house-high cores, the small stones look only. RF-3 (26 Nov 2026): the clusters still read bare because 97 per cent of the ground above the treeline is steeper than steepest (rise about 1.5 a metre, 57 degrees) and got no rock at all (2 per cent of those cells had one); the crags stand on it, more satellites, scree thicker under walls. Measured on the baked heights round the two picture spots: above the treeline the median spot has 55 rocks within 60 m, 16 of them of 1 m radius or more (the coordinator's target: 40 and 8). RF-4 (27 Nov 2026, Dave on those pictures: "really the most rocks need to be at the bottom where they should have fallen as the mountain eroded away over time"): most rocks lie at the feet (scree on ground up to scree_flat_max, the slope talus rests at, scree_clusters 12), a third as many crags on the faces, bigger rocks commoner (radius_power 1.2); measured on the baked heights: cliff feet median 63 rocks within 60 m, 21 of 1 m or more, the steep faces 27 and 10, above the treeline 20 and 7. RF-5 (27 Nov 2026, Dave with three photos of talus under cliffs: "I want some really big boulders like it should look real. some big enough to climb on and some just too big ... fill up the space with bigger boulders like 2-5 meter across boulders and then some broken rocks and smaller 1-3m chunkes in between and on the ground around them"): cores 2 to 5 m across, every size as common (radius_power 1), satellites 0.35 to 0.65 of the core; the client lays a talus of broken chunks round each big mountain rock (inventory_view _skirt_mesh: look and collision, no rows). RF-6 (27 Nov 2026, Dave on the rocks12 picture: "higher up on the hill they should be smaller, the lower they get the bigger they should be and right were it starts to transition from hill to flat ground there should be much bigger boulders. the type that make the terrain hard to traverse."): a cluster core shrinks with how far the ground falls below it within relief_reach_m (full size at up_hill[0] m, up_hill[2] of it at up_hill[1] m); where scree reaches near-flat ground (rise up to foot.flat_max) the foot band takes foot.clusters a cell, cores of radius.foot (4 to 6 m across, 3 m radius being the floor lookups' limit) and foot.satellites round each, packed: ground hard to cross on foot. RF-7 (27 Nov 2026, Dave on rocks13: "multiply the boulders numbers by like 30 and make them bigger the lower they go"; then: "we need to be careful how we code it and then work to keep it light weight"): the foot band is every scree spot (a flat-only band was a few patches), its cores foot.steep_share as big where the ground is as steep as scree_flat_max, full size at foot.flat_max and flatter; each of its rocks lies in a client-drawn field of big broken boulders (the skirt's 4th value; no rows, so no more world sync), satellites as other scree. RF-8 (27 Nov 2026, Dave: "we should be placing them wherever the should have already settled after millions of years"): steepest and scree_flat_max 0.7, about the 35 degrees loose rock rests at (they were 1.0 and 0.85, where a loose rock would long since have slid); steeper spots take crags, bedrock standing out of the face. Every rock is laid at rest and moves only when the ground under its middle is dug (server_items settle_loose_near, BoulderFall).

distribution.note: The island resource landscape (Dave 21 Nov 2026, docs/handoff/RESOURCE_DISTRIBUTION_ARCHITECTURE.md; what each value does and why: docs/design/RESOURCE_DISTRIBUTION.md, provisional RD-1..RD-12). Built once a run from the baked tiles' coarse maps by src/stream/resource_context.gd on a 64 m grid: journey (0 on the shore, 1 at the headwaters under the high ground, from the distance to the sea, the height and the high ground near), iron, copper and tin areas (the paint: each island covered to its cover share, iron most, tin least, with its own warped noise per metal so the areas overlap without rings), sources of each metal (deposit_*), and river clues below each source down its own drainage (transport_m). The server's scatter reads it: copper, tin and iron rocks only in their area or on their clue, sizes and shapes by journey, sources laid out as outcrops with fragments downhill.
distribution.rich_note: The rich layer (Dave 27 Nov 2026, the layered cake: "we need to make sure that super rich layer is right around the bottom of the mountain or on the first plateau to give people a reason to make there way up there"; BugsList 186, RD-16): rich rises with the journey to 1 at rich_journey_full, then eases a little (rich_ease_up; Dave 27 Nov: "its ok to have good resources as you go further up the mountain") once the ground is above rich_foot_up of the island's peak (over rich_band_up), so the mountain foot and first plateau are the richest and the mountain itself less so. Ore rocks (copper, tin, iron: chances by water and sizes) and sources (chance and size) read rich in place of the journey; ore rocks' shapes follow rich too (angular toward the foot); the areas, plain boulders, rock fields and pockets keep the journey. Iron cover 1.0 (was 0.9) so small iron lies by the shore too. PROVISIONAL.

first_bronze.note: PROVISIONAL RD-13 (handoff 13 bronze progression; stage 4, 21 Nov 2026). The first bronze kit a player makes: the bronze tools that replace the stone and copper ones (the Bronze - Pickaxe also opens iron ore), and the two stations the way to iron requires (Improved smelter: bellows for iron; Improved smithy: the station that works iron), whose bronze ingots, nails and hinges come from the Primitive smithy. resource_context.first_bronze_need reads every amount from recipes.json, blueprints.json and structures.json smelting (today 21 Bronze ingots: 11 Copper ore and 11 Tin ore a player). players: a full server (32, the status page's max) all starting on the one island, so the check holds for the busiest world; weapons and armour not counted (a player's choice, not the way forward).

distribution.known_sources_note: PROVISIONAL RD-14 (handoff 13: players may already know several iron locations before they can process it): the starting island must have this many sources of each metal within its route budget, else assured ones are added (up to three). Iron 3 = several; copper and tin 1 (their quantity is checked by first_bronze). Across seeds 1 to 200 on the shipped tiles (cloud mirror, before this rule) iron had 0 to 9 sources within 3 km by route, fewer than 3 in 38 seeds; this rule adds them.
distribution.ore_margin_note: PROVISIONAL RD-13: the starting island's sources within their route budgets must hold the first bronze ore this many times over in their outcrops alone (some outcrops lie in water or on ground the server skips; ore goes to other things too). Fragments and loose pieces below a source are extra.

coal.note: Coal districts and seams (handoff: coal on hillsides and near water, as seams to discover and follow). PROVISIONAL RD-9. A district is dry land on a slope (slope_min..slope_full rise per metre on the 64 m grid) within wet_reach_m of a lake, river, marsh, swamp, fen or bog (wet_classes, water_classes.json; streams cut down through coal beds and show them in their banks), where its own noise (wave_m) passes noise_cut. A seam: one candidate per seam_grid_m square, chance seam_chance x district; a coal layer thick_m thick at the ground height of its centre, length_m along the contour, into_m into the hill and out_m out. Where it meets the ground the server lays a dark coal outcrop every outcrop_every_m (radius outcrop_radius_m) with loose coal below; a shovel dig inside the layer gives per_dig coal (plus the shovel tier's extra) as well as the ground's own yield, until the seam's coal_per_m x its length is dug out (a bounded body; it does not grow back).
coal.host_note: PROVISIONAL RD-15 (handoff: use sedimentary host rock where the world supports it; stage 4, 21 Nov 2026): a seam whose centre lies in igneous or metamorphic layered rock of the baked tile (rocks.json family: granite, basalt, tuff, slate, marble) has no outcrops and no coal; sediment, shale, limestone, coal, sandstone and chalk hold it. Read by the server at the seam's centre and height once its tile is in memory (server_items._seam_host_ok); unknown rock never stops one. How many seams it keeps near spawn is a lane measure (the server log), not a cloud one.
coal.outcrop_note: 22 Nov 2026 (coordinator for Dave, gate pictures: a seam read as a few dark boulders 14 m apart): outcrops every 6 m (was 14) at radius 0.4 to 0.8 m (was 0.5 to 1.0), 1 to 3 loose coal below each (was 0 to 2), drawn near-black (inventory_view OUTCROP_LOOK), so a seam reads as a dark band along the slope with crumbs below. Outcrop coal per seam about +17% (station count x2.3, rock volume x0.51); the dig body (coal_per_m) is unchanged.
coal.first_find: A black seam of coal runs through the hillside here. Follow it into the hill.

distribution.pocket_note: Pockets (handoff: digging occasionally reveals pockets or veins of gems, crystals, gold or silver; coordinator D-ORE-1 21 Nov 2026 under Dave's rule that agents' questions go to the coordinator). PROVISIONAL RD-10. Each row: find (ore.finds), metals (the sources it goes with), journey_min..journey_max (how far inland the source is), chance per roll x (0.5 + the source's size), per_source rolls, place (source: within the source's radius x 1.2; gravel: in the river gravels 1..gravel_cells 64 m cells down its drainage), depth_m under the generated ground, r_m (a dig this close that reaches the depth opens it). An opened pocket shows as a small rock in the hole (pocket_rock: stones and grade by find) to break with a pick or the Stone Hammer. Associations: gold as placer nuggets in river gravels below sources and in quartz veins at inland copper and iron sources; silver with copper; amethyst and agate in quartz cavities; garnet in hard mountain rock (the highest sources); clear quartz (Crystal lens) in cavities.

pocket_rock.say: You dig into a pocket of %s. Break it out with a pick or the Stone Hammer.

distribution.veins_note: Gold and silver veins (R-RES-PRECIOUS, Dave 27 Nov 2026, go 28 Nov: "in veins along side the deeper iron, tin veins under the mountains or up in the mountains. they should be spread so as to entice the players to travel, make roads, build caravans and enterprise around building mines etc. also we could have gem stones and such in reasonable places or maybe they become something only discovered by a percentage chance as you mine deeper"). resource_context._veins: an iron or tin source (metals) at journey_min or farther inland (the rich layer and the mountains) starts a vein with chance x (0.5 + its size), never within gap_m of another vein's start. finds: gold or silver by weight. It runs uphill from the source's edge under the mountain for length_m: a pocket every step_m (a dig within r_m that reaches its depth opens it, as any pocket), the first outcrop_points lying on the ground as rocks with no dig (pocket_rock outcrop_*: bigger, more stones, grade x outcrop_grade), the rest buried deeper along it (depth_m, shallow end to deep end). Under each buried pocket, gem_below_m deeper, a gem with chance gem_per_m x the pocket's depth (3 m down: 18 percent); gems: [find, journey_min], one of those that fit picked at random. Same pocket save and breaking as every pocket: any pick or the Stone Hammer. Sell value only (D-ORE-1): no recipes, coins or trade. All values PROVISIONAL, docs/design/RESOURCE_DISTRIBUTION.md RD-17.

flint.note: Flint (guide finding F-02, FLINT_ORE_SPEC.md): each stone that comes off a boulder is a flint nodule instead with this chance, more near water. Bank stones (drops.json ground_scatter.bank.flint) are flint with their own chance. Flint makes the hide scraper, javelin and sickle.
